# Video script

<!-- generated by `ggh writeup` from the results bundle and committed evidence; edit SEGMENTS in src/ggh/release/writeup.py, not this file -->

About 90 seconds, 216 words of narration. Every visual is a recorded asset in `docs/assets/`. Every claim is one the results bundle or the model card makes.

| Time | Visual | Narration |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:08 | Title card over `docs/assets/screenshots/demo_answer.png`; the research-only notice on screen | Can a small open model answer a health research question only from the abstract in front of it, and show which sentences it used? Research only, not medical advice. |
| 0:08–0:20 | `docs/assets/screenshots/demo_answer.png`: an abstract with its numbered sentences, base and v2 answer cards, the cited sentence highlighted | The model is Gemma 4 E2B, tuned with LoRA on a free Kaggle T4. It reads numbered sentences and answers with a label, a short answer and the sentences it relied on. |
| 0:20–0:32 | `docs/assets/architecture.svg`, then `docs/assets/screenshots/evalkit_report_main_v2.png` | Every model is scored with EvalKit on all 1,000 expert-labelled PubMedQA questions. The score that counts: the label is right and every claim is supported by what it cites. |
| 0:32–0:47 | `docs/assets/screenshots/v1_vs_v2_citation.png`: the same answer, v1 citing the aim sentence, v2 citing the result | Version one raised label accuracy from 0.501 to 0.728, but it cited the study's aim instead of its results, so it fell below its own base on that score. |
| 0:47–1:02 | `docs/assets/headline_v2.svg`: base, v1 and v2 with their intervals | Version two was retrained on citations that each support the answer. Citation precision rose from 0.362 to 0.736. The headline did not move: 0.329 against v1's 0.331, and base is still better at 0.404. |
